summary: Re-tested M2-S04 (validation, built by metadata-builder) after the N3-F-06 repair (envelope envelopes/M2-S04/2026-09-19T15-08-49Z.json) rewrote <description> from 766 to 205 characters; every other element of the ValidationRule and package.xml are byte-identical to the run this step's first test pass (2026-09-19T14-59-39Z) covered. Ran both declared checkers verbatim from the build directory exactly as the plan wrote them: check_validation_rules.py at the plan's declared build scope (--manifest-dir artefacts), which scanned two validation rules across two files and printed 'Scanned 2 validation rule(s) across 2 file(s); 1 finding(s) detected.' with one REVIEW-severity advisory on this step's rule ('picklist logic has no explicit blank guard') -- exit 0, unaffected by the description-only repair, matching the prior tested run's output; and check_products_and_pricebooks.py at step scope (--manifest-dir artefacts/M2-S04), which exited 0 with 'No issues found.' -- this step's artefact tree carries one ValidationRule and no Product2/Pricebook2/PricebookEntry metadata, so the exit asserts nothing demonstrable about the step, recorded as a pass against the declared expectation and not as catalog validation, exactly as the prior tester recorded it. Also ran the always-on xml parse (2/2 files parse), the always-on manifest consistency check (ValidationRule named explicitly in package.xml with a file behind it, both directions consistent, no wildcard, package.xml byte-identical to the prior run), and check-outputs --hashes (ok, nothing missing/empty/malformed; the validation-rule file and deploy-order.md hashes changed from the prior tested run's stale ones, package.xml did not). All four runnable tests passed. The step's one manual acceptance test was checked against the Given/When/Then shape (all three clauses present, Then directly inspectable) and deferred verbatim to the M2 milestone gate rather than ticked. As a courtesy this run also read deploy-order.md against both Then clauses: section 2.1 now reads 'ORG-VERIFIED (2026-09-19)' with the dry-run settlement named (superseding the original UNVERIFIED marker, which is kept verbatim rather than deleted), and section 2.2 still states 'FORWARD GATE ONLY' as unresolved -- both Then-clause facts hold, but the manual test's own Given premise ('the two UNVERIFIED claims') now reads as stale phrasing against a step where one claim has since been org-verified; flagged in Process Observations rather than resolved here, since ticking or rewording a milestone-gate manual test is not this agent's role. tests/M2-S04/results.json overwritten (previous run's artefact_hashes were stale against the repaired file) with "passed": true and fresh artefact_hashes from check-outputs --hashes; M2-S04 moved built -> tested via build_plan.py set-status, called once.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran (or was correctly classified as manual), both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly -- the Step 7 HIGH row in agents/step-tester/AGENT.md. No command test was refused, no manifest exclusion had to be applied, and check-outputs reported ok with nothing missing, empty or malformed. The products-and-pricebooks checker's unproven exit 0 and the manual test's stale Given premise are reported as Process Observations rather than confidence downgrades, since neither is a refused command, a coverage-gap exclusion, nor a check-outputs problem -- the three conditions the MEDIUM row is keyed to.

process_observations.observation: The N3-F-06 description repair changed exactly one element (<description>, 766 -> 205 chars) and nothing else. Both declared checkers produced byte-identical stdout to the prior tested run, package.xml's hash is unchanged, and only the validation-rule file's and deploy-order.md's hashes moved. A repair this narrow is the reason a description-length org rejection could be fixed and re-tested without disturbing anything the first test pass already established (formula, errorDisplayField, errorMessage, manifest membership).

check_products_and_pricebooks.py's declared test on this step exits 0 with 'No issues found.' but this step's artefact tree has no Product2, Pricebook2 or PricebookEntry metadata for it to inspect -- the same finding the prior tested run and the builder's own control run recorded. The declared 'expected: exit 0' is met and is recorded as a pass, but a reader of a green test list should not infer the rule's product-catalog correctness was checked by this test.

The step's manual acceptance test opens 'Given the two UNVERIFIED (2026-09-15) claims' -- true when the test was written, but deploy-order.md section 2.1 has since been updated to 'ORG-VERIFIED (2026-09-19)', superseding rather than deleting the original UNVERIFIED text. The Then clause ('both appear verbatim with the dry-run settlement named for the first') still literally holds, because the doc keeps the original wording and adds the settlement rather than replacing it -- so this run defers the test rather than reporting it unusable. But a human reading the test's Given at the M2 gate without also reading deploy-order.md section 2.1 in full could reasonably believe both claims remain open, which they do not. This is a wording-currency question for the manual test itself, not an artefact defect, and step-tester does not edit acceptance-test text -- named here for the M2 gate and for build-doc-keeper.

set-status's full-plan validate pass printed 19 pre-existing WARNs about other steps (M1, M3, M4) shipping a cited skill's checker with no declared acceptance test for it. None name M2-S04 or its cited skills (admin/validation-rules, admin/products-and-pricebooks); they predate this run and are outside this invocation's one-step scope, so nothing was changed on their account. This matches the set the prior M2-S04 test run and the M2-S03 test run observed, confirming no new WARN was introduced by this re-test.
